verdict.rationale: incident.io documents an official MCP server that lets any MCP-capable AI assistant query incidents, analyze alerts, check who's on call and manage escalations without opening the dashboard. The changelog also notes that status pages can be updated through the agent. This is genuine first-party natural-language operation, but the documented scope covers only part of the product. missing for 10: evidence that core actions such as declaring, updating or resolving incidents, configuring workflows and schedules can be driven by natural-language commands; a native in-product natural-language command interface; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Query incidents, analyze alerts, check who's on call, manage escalations, and run deep operational analysis — all from your existing AI tools.
Ask your AI assistant about incidents, alerts, and on-call without opening the dashboard
You can now update your status page using the agent
